subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw restore a cross-machine Chrome extension relay path, retire it permanently, or first design a generic browser-backend/plugin API that can host a secure optional relay?
rationale: The issue is a real regression for managed-hosting users, but the fix would define a browser-control security boundary and public config/API surface, so automation cannot safely choose the product direction by reviving the old driver alone.

options.title: Design secure backend API plus optional relay
options.body: Add a reviewed browser backend/plugin contract and implement the relay as an explicit, scoped, audited optional capability with migration and docs.

options.title: Keep relay retired
options.body: Document that cross-machine browser control requires a node host or remote CDP and close relay restoration requests once the migration limits are explicit.

options.title: Restore legacy relay directly
options.body: Bring back `driver: "extension"` and the relay server as a compatibility path, accepting the higher security and maintenance burden.

recommendation.title: Design secure backend API plus optional relay
recommendation.body: Add a reviewed browser backend/plugin contract and implement the relay as an explicit, scoped, audited optional capability with migration and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc authored and merged the removal/migration PR that defines the current browser-driver behavior, making him the strongest initial routing owner for the restore-versus-retire decision.
